newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Graham as NZ premier may bring coalition - paper.
newsitem.headline: Graham as NZ premier may bring coalition - paper.

text.p: The Wellington newspaper The Dominion in a front page story on Monday said replacing Prime Minister Jim Bolger with Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham could clear the way for a coalition between the National Party and New Zealand First.

After Saturday's inconclusive general election, the conservative National Party with 44 seats is vying with the centre-left Labour Party to win the support of nationalist NZ First with its 17 seats to form a government.
Speculation that Peters might try to deal with Graham at Bolger's expense heightened after reports that Peters' close advisers had been desperate on Sunday to track down Graham's phone number.
There is a wide belief in Maoridom that a Graham-Peters leadership in a coalition would overcome many of the traditional Maori prejudices against National, the paper said.
NZ First swept to victory in all the Maori seats on Saturday and had their most solid support base among Maori.
Graham had won much goodwill from Maori through his handling of treaty settlements, the paper said.
Maori political commentators suggested NZ First's best hope of dealing with National without antagonising Maori support would be if Graham was involved, it said.

Peters' dislike of Bolger was no secret and two months ago he told Bolger not to try ringing him after the election in an effort to retain his job. Peters had softened his stance since then," it added.
Bolger, commenting on Radio New Zealand said the newspaper's story was speculation.
